# simpledir

> Named directory shortcuts for the shell. The next zoxide: no frecency
> database, no daemon, no dependencies. One JSON file of `name -> path`, and
> two commands split by what they do to you.

`sd` moves you and only ever reads your config. `sdcfg` changes things and never
changes your directory. Both names are the same file; the program decides which
half it is by the name it was invoked as (`argv[0]`).

Complements, does not replace, [zoxide](https://github.com/ajeetdsouza/zoxide).

## Docs

- [README.md](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/blob/main/README.md): full documentation
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/blob/main/AGENTS.md): notes for coding agents working on this repository
- [CONTRIBUTORS.md](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/blob/main/CONTRIBUTORS.md): authorship and how to contribute
- [LICENSE](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/blob/main/LICENSE): MIT

## Install

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/main/install.sh | bash
```

The installer checks for Python 3.8+, installs it with yay, pacman or mise (in
that order) if missing, downloads the release asset into `~/.local/bin/sd`,
symlinks `sdcfg` to it, and appends a guarded wrapper block to `~/.bashrc` or
`~/.zshrc` (chosen from `$SHELL`). Re-running refreshes the block and keeps a
backup. `bash install.sh --uninstall` reverses all of it.

From source: `git clone … && make install`.

## Commands

`sd` — moves you, reads the config:

```
sd <alias>                 jump (equivalent to `sd print <alias>`)
sd -                       previous directory
sd                         $HOME
sd /some/path              a raw path, cd'd as-is
sd ls [<query>] [--long]   list jumpable aliases; --names one per line; --json the config shape
sd print <alias[/sub]>     print the directory without cd'ing
sd suggest [--top N] [--json]   mine shell history for directories worth naming
sd i [<query>]             interactive picker; fzf if installed, numbered list otherwise
```

`sdcfg` — changes things, never moves you:

```
sdcfg add [<name>] [<path>]   bind; name defaults to the directory basename, path to $PWD; --force to overwrite; --keep-symlinks to skip resolution
sdcfg rm <name>               remove an alias
sdcfg rename <old> <new>      rename, keeping the path; --force to overwrite
sdcfg import <dir>            bind every subdirectory of a tree; --depth (default 1), --prefix, --force, --hidden, --dry-run, --keep-symlinks
sdcfg bind [--top N] [--dry-run]   create aliases from what `sd suggest` found
sdcfg edit [<editor>]         open the config in $EDITOR, creating an empty one if absent
sdcfg update                  check for a newer release, ask, then install; --check reports only (exit 1 if one exists); --yes skips the prompt
sdcfg uninstall               remove the install; --purge also deletes ~/.simpledir and every alias; --yes skips the prompt
sdcfg doctor                  report config, dead aliases, shell wiring and PATH problems; exit 1 if any
sdcfg completions bash|zsh    print a shell completion script
sdcfg init                    print the shell wrapper to append to a shell rc file
```

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` unknown alias or user error, `2` argument parsing
error (argparse).

All flags are long-form only; there are no short aliases.

Reaching for the wrong half is a usage error (exit 2) and gets a pointer:
`sd add` prints `did you mean 'sdcfg add'? sd only reads your config.`

An alias argument may carry a path suffix: `dots/src` resolves to `<dots>/src`.
Suffixes are normalized with `normpath`, so `dots/src/..` and `dots/` both work.
The shell wrapper also accepts a raw path: `sd /some/path` just `cd`s.

An exact alias name always wins. If there is no exact match, a **unique name
prefix** is accepted: `hy` jumps to `hypr`. Two or more candidates is an error
that lists them, never a guess.

## History mining

`sd suggest` reads `~/.bash_history`, `~/.zsh_history` and the fish history files
(`SIMPLEDIR_HISTORY=/path` adds another file), and understands bash plain lines,
zsh extended history (`: <time>:<dur>;<cmd>`) and fish (`- cmd: <cmd>`). It
extracts directories from `cd`, `pushd` and `z`, including `cd a b` and `cd -x /p`,
and ignores bare `cd`, `cd -`, `~`, and anything that is not an existing
directory. `cd` only counts at the start of a command or after a separator
(`&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, …), so `echo cd /tmp` is not a suggestion.

Relative history targets (`cd Projects`) are resolved against `$HOME`, since the
directory they were typed from is not recorded anywhere. They are skipped when
that path does not exist.

It counts how often each directory appears, drops the ones already bound, ranks
by frequency, and prints a list plus ready-to-paste `sdcfg add` lines. `sdcfg
bind` creates them, naming each after its own directory and de-duplicating
collisions with a numeric suffix.

## Symlinks

`add` and `import` resolve symlinks unless `--keep-symlinks` is given, which
stores `os.path.abspath` instead of `Path.resolve()`. Reading an alias always
uses `as_stored()`, which never resolves: a path bound with `--keep-symlinks`
stays symlinked for the life of the alias.

## Configuration

Path: `~/.simpledir/config.json`. Override the directory with the
`SIMPLEDIR_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable. The file is plain JSON and safe to
edit by hand.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "aliases": {
    "dots": "/home/you/dotfiles",
    "hypr": "/home/you/.config/hypr"
  }
}
```

Schema: `version` is an integer, currently `1`. `aliases` maps a non-empty alias
name to an absolute directory path. Writes are atomic: temporary file plus
`os.replace`.

## Shell wrapper

A subprocess cannot change the calling shell's cwd, so `sdcfg init` prints a
function that performs the `cd`, using `sd print` to resolve the path. The
function intercepts only bare aliases; `ls`, `print`, `suggest` and `i` are
forwarded to the binary without changing directory, as is any `-flag`.

- no arguments: `cd $HOME`
- `-`: `cd $OLDPWD`
- an absolute path or one starting with `~`: `cd` straight to it

Functions rather than shell aliases, because bash expands aliases only in
interactive shells.

## Behavior on errors

- unknown alias: message with substring and `difflib` suggestions, exit `1`
- alias or alias-with-suffix resolving to a missing directory: `jump` refuses and
  explains how to rebind; `ls` tags it `[missing]`
- duplicate alias: refused unless `--force`, for both `add` and `rename`
- corrupt or unreadable config: explains the problem, suggests removal, does not
  silently reset
- `ls` with no aliases: usage hint on stderr, exit `1`
- `ls <query>` with no match: says so, exit `1`
- unknown flag, or a verb belonging to the other command: argparse usage error,
  exit `2`, with a pointer to the right command
- `update` when GitHub is unreachable: says so, exit `1`
- `update` never replaces a binary with a same-version or unidentifiable download
- `uninstall` without a terminal and without `--yes`: refuses rather than
  guessing, exit `1`

## Update mechanism

`update` fetches `https://api.github.com/repos/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/releases/latest`,
compares `tag_name` against `VERSION`, and on a newer tag downloads the release
asset `sd`, runs it with `--version` to confirm identity and version, then
writes it next to the target and `os.replace`s it into place.

Additionally, `sd ls` and `sdcfg add` may print a one-line nudge to stderr when a
newer release is known. It is suppressed when stderr is not a terminal, when
`SIMPLEDIR_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` is set, when the cache in
`~/.simpledir/update-check.json` is younger than 24 hours, and never on the
`sd print` path.

Environment variables:

```
SIMPLEDIR_CONFIG_DIR       config directory                (default ~/.simpledir)
SIMPLEDIR_NO_UPDATE_CHECK  set to anything to disable update checks
SIMPLEDIR_BIN              override the path `update` writes to, and `uninstall` removes
SIMPLEDIR_RC               the only rc file `uninstall` and `doctor` will touch
SIMPLEDIR_HISTORY          an extra history file for `sd suggest` to read
SIMPLEDIR_NO_FZF           set to anything to make `sd i` skip fzf
SIMPLEDIR_UPDATE_URL       override the release API URL (used by the test suite)
SIMPLEDIR_UPDATE_ASSET_URL override the downloaded asset URL (used by the test suite)
```

## Uninstall

`sdcfg uninstall` removes the binary at `install_target()` and strips every
`# >>> simpledir >>>` … `# <<< simpledir <<<` span from the rc files in
`rc_candidates()`, rewriting each through a staged file and leaving a
`<rc>.bak.<timestamp>` backup. Aliases in `~/.simpledir` are preserved unless
`--purge` is given. Deleting the running script is safe on unix.

`SIMPLEDIR_RC`, when set, is exclusive: it names the only rc file considered.
Without it, candidates are guessed from `$SHELL` plus `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`
and `~/.config/fish/config.fish`.

## Version history

- 5.0.0 — split into two commands: `sd` (moves, read-only) and `sdcfg` (writes,
  never moves). Long-form flags only; the short forms are gone. `suggest --bind`
  became `sdcfg bind`. Breaking change to the command surface; the config format
  is unchanged at `version: 1`.
- 4.0.0 — `suggest` (history mining), `i` (interactive picker, fzf optional),
  `add`/`import --keep-symlinks`, and unique-prefix matching on jump. Reading an
  alias no longer resolves symlinks.
- 3.1.0 — `uninstall`: removes its own binary and the wrapper block, keeping
  aliases unless `--purge`.
- 3.0.0 — one-command `curl | bash` installer, `update` with verification and
  atomic self-install, a quiet once-a-day update nudge, `import`, `doctor`,
  downloadable release assets.
- 1.0.0 — `add`, `rm`, `ls`, `jump`, `init`, the shell wrapper, typo
  suggestions, atomic config writes.
- 2.0.0 — path suffixes, `rename`, `add` with fewer arguments, `edit`, `ls`
  filtering, `--names`, `--json`, shell completions.

## Development

```
make test     # 235 assertions, runs real bash subprocesses
make assets   # build dist/ (sd + install.sh, mode 755)
make release  # tag from VERSION, push, publish with assets
vhs docs/demo.tape   # re-record docs/demo.gif (needs vhs and ttyd)
```

Repository layout:

```
sd                 the entire tool, one executable file. installed as `sd` with `sdcfg` symlinked to it
install.sh         the curl | bash installer
tests/run.sh       test suite, plain bash
docs/demo.tape     vhs script that produces docs/demo.gif
packaging/PKGBUILD Arch package definition
packaging/nix/     a nixpkgs expression
Makefile           install / uninstall / test / assets / release targets
```
